title: Digit Sum
story: Take any number. Add its digits. Take the new number. Add ITS digits. Repeat. You eventually reach a single digit — the 'digital root.' 12345 → 1+2+3+4+5 = 15 → 1+5 = 6. This simple operation powers checksums, numerology, and divisibility tricks.
why: Digit sum teaches the fundamental pattern of extracting and processing individual digits using modulo and division — a pattern used in countless algorithms.
analogy: Peeling an onion layer by layer: each digit is a layer, and you peel from the outside (rightmost digit) using % 10, revealing the next layer with /. The digit sum is the pile of all peels combined. The digital root is boiling it down to a single essence.
try_it: Riddle: A number equals 4 times its digit sum. Find it. Hint: try numbers 10-99. Also check which numbers are divisible by 3 using digit sum. Verify that digital_root(n) == n % 9 (with the 9 exception) for numbers 1-100.
tips: `% 10` gets the last digit, `/ 10` removes it — the two-step pattern of digit ops
The digital root has a mathematical shortcut: n % 9 (with special case for 0)
Digit ops work on the decimal representation — change the base for binary, octal, etc.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to handle n=0 — its digit sum is 0, but the while loop never runs
Using `n = n / 10` inside the loop but then checking the original n afterwards
Confusing digit sum with digit count — sum vs count are different accumulations
